propositions: The enrich-drain advisory lock is held across no-timeout LLM calls (437s/131s observed), causing every concurrent drain child to skip with lock-held and creating structural single-flight bottleneck below the enqueue rate.

Restructuring drain() into three phases (collect/enrich/finalize) with lock released before LLM calls reduces per-item lock cost from 87.4s to 9.8s (~9x) and enables up to 3 concurrent drainers processing ~20 items per batch.
Stale-at-writeback revalidation via content-hash snapshot prevents emission of outdated enrichments; stale entries are re-enqueued with soak 0 and counted as stale_skipped.
Effective batch cap is lease-derived (max(1, lease_ttl_s // 40) = 22 at default 15-min lease) to prevent lease expiry mid-run and bound crash blast radius.

Concurrency guard limits live-lease drainers to 3 distinct drainer_ids in the collect phase; a 4th drainer skips with concurrency-cap; subsequent drain children become productive concurrent workers instead of all skipping.

Lease-expiry recovery and existing failure disposition (transient -> retry, permanent CHANGE_INPUT -> tombstone) remain unchanged; store write lock semantics and queue event schema (ENQUEUE/CLAIM/DONE) are preserved.
